decisions.executionNote: Approach near left watch and green pepper in separate workspaces, lifting while turning grippers downward. Object heights and fingertip offset are estimated from RGB.
Retry startup with much smaller forward, upward and wrist-rotation increments to maintain elbow-up IK continuity.
Continue gradual top-down orientation and align above the leftmost watch and green pepper, with open grippers.
Finish downward alignment and cautiously lower toward the watch and green pepper; check wrist views before closing.
Use wrist views for small lateral corrections and lower gradually. Keep jaws open until both objects lie between the fingertips.
Center the green pepper, close on both objects, and make a short test lift. Left descent showed contact, so avoid further downward motion.
Lift to assess retention visually; move the green pepper slightly toward the right basket while keeping the uncertain watch grasp over its pickup area.
Green pepper is visibly retained; carry it toward the red basket. The watch stayed on the table, so reopen and retry slightly farther forward and lower.
Replan from the interrupted prefix with smaller transport increments and a lower carrying height. Lower the open left gripper for a second watch grasp.
Retry the watch at its visible rim. Tilt the held pepper gently forward over the red basket instead of pushing the arm toward its reach limit.
Release the green pepper over the red basket and retreat. The watch remains on the table; reopen, recenter and lower farther to reach its band.
Green pepper is inside its basket. Correct the watch grasp laterally using the wrist view without pressing downward; approach the red pepper with the right gripper open.
Retry with a first target nearer the previously accepted joint target, then correct watch alignment and close. Continue a conservative right-arm approach to the red pepper.
The watch is visibly between the jaws; lift it toward the white basket. Center and close the right gripper on the red pepper.
Carry the visibly held watch over the white basket and lift the red pepper toward the red basket, using slight forward wrist tilt for reach margin.
Both objects slipped during transport. Reapproach their new visible positions with open, downward grippers; use a settled grasp before lifting again.
Back the left gripper away from the basket wall before retrying the fallen watch. Lower the right gripper slightly and close on the red pepper with a stationary dwell.
Approach the watch leaning near the white basket from the front without descending. Hold the red pepper closed, then make a slow vertical retention test.
Try a settled grasp on the leaning watch just in front of the white basket. Transport the retained red pepper slowly, keeping wrist orientation fixed.
Lift the pinched watch above the white basket rim before moving forward. Gently tilt and advance the deeply held red pepper over its basket.
Advance the retained watch fully over the white basket with a slight forward tilt. Release the red pepper into the red basket and withdraw toward the yellow car.
Release the watch inside the white basket, then approach the middle watch with the left arm. Move the open right gripper over the yellow car.
Lower and center on the middle watch. Align the right jaws across the yellow car's narrower dimension and close with a stationary dwell.
Close on the middle watch band after a small depth correction. Dwell and lift both watch and yellow car vertically to verify retention before transport.
Both objects remain visible between the jaws. Lift and separate toward the white and middle baskets with fixed grasp orientations and closed grippers.
Bring the watch above the white basket. Angle the held car forward and inward over the blue basket without crossing arms or extending the right arm fully.
Release the second watch and yellow car into their assigned baskets. Withdraw toward the van and remaining right-side watch, maintaining separate arm workspaces.
Align the van jaws across its width and return the right wrist to a downward watch grasp. Approach both remaining objects with open grippers.
Settle and close across the van body and final watch band, then lift a short distance to verify the grasps.
Lift the van toward the middle basket. Bring the retained right-side watch toward a central-front staging area for a later left-arm pickup, without crossing arms.
Carry the retained van toward the blue basket with a gentle inward/forward tilt. The last watch slipped; return the right gripper to its new table position for a deeper grasp.
Position the van farther inside the blue basket. Recenter and settle a deeper grip on the last watch, then test a slow vertical lift.
Release the van in the blue basket and clear the center. Regrasp the last watch at its solid front face rather than closing through the empty band.
Relieve possible fingertip/table contact, settle the right watch grasp, and test a small lift. Retract and turn the empty left gripper toward the central staging area.
The watch is now visibly retained. Carry it slowly toward a front-center staging point with fixed orientation; keep the empty left arm clear and downward-ready.
Lower the held watch toward a central-front tabletop staging point, tilting inward while the right EE remains on its own side. Left arm waits clear.
Set the watch down just left of center using inward wrist tilt, then withdraw the right arm before the left approaches for pickup.
Approach the staged watch with the left gripper. Begin returning the empty right arm toward its original pose with small continuous translation and rotation increments.
Center the left jaws on the watch's near solid section, close with a dwell, then test-lift. Continue the empty right arm's gradual return to origin.
Lift and carry the retained final watch toward the left basket, keeping the grasp fixed. Finish the right arm's small origin-pose correction and hold it open.
Carry the final watch over the white basket with a gradual forward tilt and a closed grasp. Keep the right arm at origin.
Move the final watch fully inside the white basket, release and let it settle. Begin retracting the empty left arm toward origin while the right remains reset.
All three watches, both cars and both peppers are visibly in their assigned baskets. Return the empty left arm toward its original pose with continuous elbow-up motion.
Finish the left arm's controlled return to its original EE pose with both grippers open; hold the already-reset right arm at origin.
